title: Doppler shift from a moving source

walkthrough: The quantity is observed frequency.
The cause is relative motion between a wave source and an observer.
Combine these into the controlled definition.

ai_rubric.observable: States that observed frequency changes.
States that the change is caused by relative motion between a wave source and an observer.

evidence.evidence_gap: This is the required direct retrieval from the completed previous lesson.

hints: Recall the square relationship from Lesson 8.
Apply it to a factor of two.
walkthrough: For a progressive wave, intensity is proportional to amplitude squared.
An amplitude factor of 2 gives an intensity factor of 2²=4.
Select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C: the intensity becomes four times as large.

hints: Connect spacing to arrivals per second.
walkthrough: An approaching source moves towards each new front before emitting the next.
Wavefront spacing ahead becomes smaller.
More fronts arrive per second, so observed frequency is higher.
Select A.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A: smaller wavefront spacing and higher observed frequency.

hints: Separate properties set by the source arrangement from the property set by the medium.
walkthrough: Recession changes the wavefront spacing and arrival rate.
The unchanged stationary air fixes the propagation speed.
Therefore the speed of sound remains unchanged, so select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C: the speed of sound through the air remains unchanged.

walkthrough: During approach, the cyclist moves forward between successive emissions.
The wavefronts ahead are closer together.
More reach the person each second, so the observed frequency is higher.

ai_rubric.observable: States that successive wavefronts ahead of the approaching source are closer together.
States that more wavefronts reach the stationary person each second.
Concludes that the observed frequency is higher.

hints: Reverse the causal chain after the source passes.
walkthrough: During recession, the source moves away between emissions.
Wavefronts reaching the person are farther apart and arrive less often.
The observed frequency is lower.

ai_rubric.observable: States that wavefronts reaching the person are farther apart and arrive less often during recession.
Concludes that the observed frequency is lower.

evidence.evidence_gap: Mapped evidence supports wavefront and frequency reasoning; the original diagram-construction task deepens representation demand.

hints: Each front stays centred on its emission position.
An earlier front has travelled for longer.
walkthrough: Centre one front on each of S1 to S4.
Give earlier fronts larger radii because they have travelled longer at the same speed.
Check that fronts crowd on the right and spread on the left.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws successive wavefronts centred on the four emission positions, with earlier fronts having larger radii.
Shows wavefronts closer together ahead on the right and farther apart behind on the left.

hints: Identify which observer is ahead of the source.
walkthrough: P is ahead of the right-moving source, where fronts are compressed.
Q is behind, where fronts are spread.
Therefore spacing at P is smaller than at Q.

ai_rubric.observable: States that wavefront spacing at P is smaller than at Q.
Links the comparison to P being ahead of and Q being behind the right-moving source.

walkthrough: Closer fronts at P arrive more often.
Wider fronts at Q arrive less often.
Thus P detects a higher frequency than Q.

ai_rubric.observable: States that P detects a higher frequency than Q.
Explains the comparison using the greater wavefront arrival rate at P.

evidence.evidence_gap: The Doppler reasoning is mapped; use of v=fλ is a deliberate earlier-module dependency.

walkthrough: Use f=v/λ.
Substitute f=330/0.60.
The frequency is 550 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses f=v/λ with 330 m s⁻¹ and 0.60 m.
Obtains 550 Hz.

hints: Keep the same wave speed and use the spacing behind.
walkthrough: Use f=v/λ again.
Substitute f=330/0.75.
The frequency is 440 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses f=v/λ with 330 m s⁻¹ and 0.75 m.
Obtains 440 Hz.

hints: State what remains fixed by the medium.
walkthrough: Source motion compresses fronts ahead to 0.60 m and spreads them behind to 0.75 m.
With the same 330 m s⁻¹ speed, these spacings give 550 Hz and 440 Hz.
The changed spacing changes arrivals per second, while every front still travels through the air at 330 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: States that source motion changes wavefront spacing, making it smaller ahead and larger behind.
Uses the calculated 550 Hz and 440 Hz values, or their comparison, to link spacing to arrival frequency.
States that the sound speed through the unchanged air remains 330 m s⁻¹.

later_learning_excluded: moving-source Doppler formula and denominator sign
